identity.name: Ajay Kumar DRB
identity.title: Frontend-focused Full Stack Developer
identity.tagline: Frontend-focused Full Stack Engineer who enjoys turning ambiguous problems into practical software products.

hero.missionDescription: From Mechanical Engineering to software craftsmanship — building scalable full-stack products across React, Node.js, APIs, databases, and integrations.

philosophy: He does not want to just write code for the sake of writing code. He wants to understand the problem, why it exists, what the user or business actually needs, and how software can make that process easier, faster, more reliable, or automated.

careerChapters.title: Before Software
careerChapters.subtitle: Mechanical Engineering to First Spark
careerChapters.description: Chose Mechanical Engineering without a clear path into software. First exposure to Python in the first year of engineering opened a door. Curiosity about how programs work and why different technologies exist gradually pulled him toward web development. Graduated with First Class with Distinction (GPA 8.66).
highlights: First exposure to Python and programming fundamentals
Developed curiosity about how software systems work
Learned to think analytically about complex systems
Graduated First Class with Distinction — GPA 8.66

careerChapters.title: The Side Mission
careerChapters.subtitle: Freelance Mathematics Expert at Chegg India
careerChapters.description: Ran alongside college and early professional work as a freelance gig. Solved 200+ mathematics questions for students across Algebra, Calculus, Discrete Maths, Statistics, PDEs, and more. Developed the habit of breaking complex problems into clear, understandable steps — a skill that carried directly into software engineering.
highlights: Solved 200+ mathematics questions across multiple disciplines
Algebra, Calculus, Discrete Maths, Statistics, PDEs, Probability
Supported students from CSE, Mechanical, and other programs
Built strong problem-decomposition and clear explanation skills

careerChapters.title: Learning How Software Fails
careerChapters.subtitle: QA Engineering at Chella Software
careerChapters.description: First professional software role. Tested enterprise financial software — functional testing, regression testing, reproducing production issues, and collaborating with developers to validate fixes. After around a year, the desire to build rather than only find bugs became the driving reason to move into development.
highlights: Functional and regression testing on enterprise financial software
Reproducing production issues and validating fixes
Collaborating with development teams on software quality
Developed a mindset for edge cases, reliability, and reproducibility

careerChapters.title: Building the Foundation
careerChapters.subtitle: MERN Bootcamp at HCL GUVI Zen
careerChapters.description: After leaving QA, enrolled in a dedicated MERN Stack Bootcamp through HCL GUVI Zen. Expanded skills across React, Next.js, Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, MySQL, and Tailwind CSS. The bootcamp's placement program connected him directly to Konnectify.
highlights: MERN Stack Bootcamp — GUVI Zen (2023–2024)
React, Next.js, Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, MySQL
Tailwind CSS, Bootstrap, full-stack project workflow
Bootcamp placement led directly to Konnectify role

careerChapters.title: Learning by Building
careerChapters.subtitle: Personal Projects and Real Confidence
careerChapters.description: Used this period to build personal full-stack applications, learn backend engineering, work with databases and authentication, and deploy real projects. The key realization: given a problem statement, Ajay could reason about it, design a software approach, build it, and ship it.
highlights: Built and deployed full-stack projects (ZapCart, SystemMapper)
Strengthened React, Node.js, MongoDB, PostgreSQL skills
Deployed real applications on Netlify and Vercel
Moved from knowing tech to building working products independently

careerChapters.title: Production Engineering
careerChapters.subtitle: Startup Full-Stack at Konnectify
careerChapters.description: Joined a workflow-automation SaaS startup (similar to Zapier) as a frontend developer. In a 5-person engineering team, worked across frontend, backend, database, integrations, and testing. Contributed to two major product revamps. Built workflow builder features, event logging, Stripe billing, user/access modules, and authentication systems.
highlights: Workflow builder: Paths, Repeaters, Code Blocks, Delays
Stripe billing with multi-currency support (USD, EUR, INR)
RSA/OAuth authentication and user access management
Freshsales and Freshdesk proof-of-concept integrations
React, NestJS, PostgreSQL across frontend and backend

projects.title: SystemMapper
projects.description: Ajay's most ambitious personal project. Accepts public GitHub repositories, parses code, identifies structure and dependencies, and visualizes them as interactive nodes and edges. Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, and C#. Deployed and working — AI-assisted analysis features are in progress.
highlights: Analyzes public GitHub repositories
Parses JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, C#
Interactive node-edge visualization of codebase structure
AI-assisted code analysis features in progress

projects.title: ZapCart
projects.tagline: MERN e-commerce platform with admin dashboard
projects.description: A full-stack e-commerce platform built on the MERN stack. Features a role-based admin dashboard, dynamic product filtering, centralized cart state via Redux Toolkit, and PayPal payment integration.
highlights: Role-based admin dashboard
Dynamic product filtering
Redux Toolkit for centralized cart state
PayPal API payment integration

projects.title: Python Interview Cookbook
projects.description: An open-source reference guide for interview preparation. Covers Python language concepts, standard library, algorithmic patterns, and interview-preparation material. Demonstrates Ajay's interest in Python, algorithms, and learning through documentation.
highlights: Python language concepts and standard library
Algorithmic patterns for interview prep
Open-source and hosted on GitHub Pages
Learning through documentation and teaching

projects.title: Golden Gauge
projects.tagline: Real-time gold price calculator with live market rates
projects.description: An early full-stack project that connects user input (gold quantity, karat, currency) to a backend API flow to fetch live market rates and calculate results. Important as Ajay's first project connecting frontend, backend, APIs, and a real-world use case.
highlights: Live gold rate API integration
Frontend to Backend to API data flow
First full-stack project connecting real-world data
User inputs: quantity, karat, and currency

contact.headline: Let's build something worth shipping.
contact.subtext: Open to full-time roles and collaborative projects across frontend, full-stack, and product engineering.

strengths.label: Full-Stack Breadth
strengths.description: Can move across frontend, backend, database, integrations, and testing instead of treating frontend as an isolated discipline.

strengths.label: Frontend Strength
strengths.description: React and Next.js are his strongest and most enjoyable development areas — from UI architecture to state management and performance.

strengths.label: Problem Solving
strengths.description: Enjoys taking an unfamiliar requirement, understanding the problem, exploring possible approaches, and implementing a working solution.

strengths.label: Product Thinking
strengths.description: Prefers to question what problem is being solved and whether there's a simpler or more useful approach before implementing.

strengths.label: QA Mindset
strengths.description: QA background helps think about edge cases, reproducibility, regressions, and whether a feature actually works as expected.

strengths.label: Independent Ownership
strengths.description: Personal projects demonstrate ability to take an idea from concept to deployment without depending on a large engineering organization.
